narrative: Your predicted probability of leaving is 62%, meaning the model views you as more likely than not to depart. In this decision, that retention risk is why you are denied a promotion, though it is not a certainty and does not use your gender, age or health status. The strongest driver was that you reported other job opportunities; this pushed the prediction toward leaving and stands out because only about 23% of employees predicted to stay had such opportunities. Your overall experience of 1–5 years was the second most influential factor, but it worked in the opposite direction, pulling toward staying; this is a common profile, with about half of stayers in that range, yet it was not enough to offset the other risks. Your other-sector background was third and pushed toward leaving; about 22% of stayers work in this sector. Next, you and your manager should discuss your career path, internal moves and what would keep you engaged. The organization should also review whether promotion decisions should rest so heavily on a leave prediction and consider retention support, clearer promotion criteria and development opportunities rather than treating the forecast as final.
